description: A single definition of the consumers the supplied Microsoft app serves on this build (email always; calendar when the calendar package is present) is read by setup, consent-time binding, reconciliation and status surfaces; no call site hard-codes ['email'] for the platform app.
prdRefs: The platform app declares what it serves

description: configureMicrosoftEmailPlatformApplication creates the platform profile with the served capabilities and a display name that does not say Email.
prdRefs: The platform app declares what it serves

description: writeMicrosoftEmailAdminConsent binds every served consumer that has no binding when the consented profile is the platform profile, never replaces an existing binding to another profile, and is unchanged for tenant-owned profiles.
prdRefs: The platform app declares what it serves

description: Email-specific names on the platform setup action and pending-consent creator are renamed where mechanical, otherwise marked with a LEVERAGE: friction comment.
prdRefs: The platform app declares what it serves

description: Idempotent, concurrency-safe reconcile-on-use adds missing served capabilities and missing served-consumer bindings to a tenant's consented, non-archived platform profile, with the no-override rule, and skips profiles pending consent.
Reconciliation runs from the calendar readiness path and the Microsoft profile status path.
getMicrosoftCalendarSetupStatus returns the credential source (supplied app or tenant-owned app) and whether the supplied app is offered on this deployment.
prdRefs: Calendar readiness knows the credential source

description: Calendar profile resolution uses the shared resolver, or the fork gains the needed fields with LEVERAGE: pattern markers at both copies.
prdRefs: Calendar readiness knows the credential source

description: Providers > Microsoft supplied-app ready banner covers email and calendar with 'Connect a mailbox' and (EE) 'Connect a calendar' actions, and the service-to-app list shows the supplied app for Outlook Calendar.
Calendar form on the supplied app replaces the Entra app registration instructions in 'Before you connect' with supplied-app copy; tenant-owned app copy is unchanged.
Calendar form not-configured state links to the provider setup entry and describes the supplied-app path when it is offered.
The calendar OAuth callback classifies Microsoft consent-required and admin-approval-required errors into a distinct error code.
The calendar form shows the admin-approval message for that error code, with the admin consent link only for users who can manage Microsoft provider settings.
Providers > Microsoft offers 'Approve calendar access' (admin consent URL) for a platform profile.
prdRefs: Calendar permissions on the shared app registration (outside the codebase)

description: New and changed strings are added to the calendar and integrations locale files.
Integration setup docs state that Outlook Calendar works with the supplied app on hosted and that a customer Entra app is optional.
